title: Western North Pacific front shifts changed winter salinity but little density; the sigma0 26.5 outcrop lightened off the T-S line, O2 at 160-180 E followed only that part, and local Ekman and E-P fail
abstract: Question: what made the late-winter surface of the western North Pacific (box W, 36-48 N, 145 E-180) lighter, so that the sigma0 26.5 outcrop shrank and oxygen (O2) on 26.5 fell at 160 E-180? Approach: pre-registered tests of local Ekman salt advection and local evaporation minus precipitation (NCEP/NCAR R1 fluxes, damped-integrator response), of subarctic source-water freshening (12,003 new World Ocean Database casts at 30-60 N) and of a meridional front shift (latitude of the late-winter SST front from OISST 1982-2025 and HadISST 1958-2025), with annual fixed-effects series of 104,079 late-winter casts. Results: Ekman advection correlates negatively with 1996-2025 salinity (r = -0.22, surrogate p = 0.67) and E-P gives none of the 2006-2017 freshening; both pre-registered tests failed. Salinity follows the front latitude (OISST r = 0.46, p = 0.019; HadISST r = 0.59, p < 0.001), and the northward shift after 2018 gives 43-85% of the 2018-2025 salinity rise, but the front was not further south in 2006-2017, when salinity was 0.113 lower than in 1965-1984. Front shifts are density-compensated: per degree north (detrended), W is 0.63-0.79 deg C warmer and 0.070-0.093 saltier, a net sigma0 change of only -0.030 to -0.035 kg/m3. The outcrop lightening (-0.081 kg/m3 in 2006-2017, -0.135 in 2018-2025) is off the 1950-1995 temperature-salinity line (-0.096 and -0.083). Added tests: within-type O2 at 36-46 N, 160 E-180 follows this off-line density (r = 0.68, surrogate p = 0.002; detrended r = 0.45, p = 0.003) and not the along-line part (r = -0.07) or the front latitude (r = 0.20, p = 0.63); fitted on 1958-1999, the off-line model predicts 2000-2025 O2 with RMSE 11.9 umol/kg against 14.5 for persistence. Ship-only and Argo-only series agree. Interpretation: frontal migration moves water along the T-S line and leaves the ventilated density classes in place; the outcrop was lost because winter water became fresher at fixed temperature (1994-2017) and then warmer at fixed salinity (2018-2025), and O2 follows that change. About 40% of the 2006-2017 freshening agrees with fresher Kuroshio and subarctic source water; local fluxes do not explain it. Limitations: local budget terms only (no geostrophic, eddy or entrainment terms); NCEP precipitation disagrees with GPCP; SST front index shares the warming trend before detrending; O2 tests were added after the pre-registered tests and use the O2 series of sci:bfaf6c90; few 50-60 N winter casts.

citations.reason: Uses its late-winter cast table, extraction and series code and its region-C O2 series. Extends its result that O2 follows the W surface density: O2 follows the off-T-S-line part of that density, not the front-shift part.

It found that climate-mode indices do not explain the 2006-2017 freshening and left Ekman, E-P and geostrophic causes open. This work tests local Ekman and E-P (they fail) and the front shift (it does not explain the freshening).
Outcrop loss ahead of the CMIP6 forced path, half from freshening that models lack; this work finds the freshening is off the T-S line and not a front shift or local flux.
